title: ChatGPT-Assisted Lesson Planning for Children’s STEAM Arts Education: An Experimental Study on Benefits, Challenges, Methods, and a Prompt Framework
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT can improve lesson planning for children’s STEAM arts education, with a specific focus on teacher-facing generative AI support rather than student tutoring or direct student text generation. The authors argue that lesson planning in children’s art and STEAM contexts is time-consuming and resource-intensive, especially when teachers must integrate interdisciplinary content, age-appropriate materials, and safety considerations. They investigate whether ChatGPT can help teachers generate, refine, and optimize lesson plans more efficiently and with higher quality.

The study was conducted with 13 children’s art teachers and 6 university professors in China. In Experiment 1, teachers created lesson plans using both traditional methods and ChatGPT-assisted methods for the same thematic lesson topic (“Color Art”) for K3 children aged 7–9. Teachers used GPT-4o and were guided by a prompt framework developed by the researchers. In Experiment 2, professors blind-rated the lesson plans using a rubric adapted from the 5E Inquiry Lesson Plan model across six dimensions, including introduction, teaching method, practical method, interdisciplinarity, after-class work, and core competencies. The study combined teacher questionnaires, interviews, ChatGPT interaction logs, observation notes, and professor ratings.

Findings suggest that ChatGPT improved lesson-planning efficiency, reduced planning time, and helped teachers generate richer content, images, and interdisciplinary ideas. Teachers generally rated ChatGPT positively and reported willingness to continue using it. However, they also identified important limitations: outputs could be overly idealized, insufficiently practical for day-to-day classrooms, and sometimes unsafe or poorly adapted to the age group. The authors conclude that ChatGPT is best understood as a collaborative tool for teacher-facing lesson planning, not a replacement for educators, and they propose a structured prompt framework to support more effective use in art education.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI chatbot / large language model system used for text generation, planning support, and interactive prompting.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by teachers to assist with lesson planning for children's STEAM arts education, including generating, refining, checking, and optimizing lesson plans and related content/resources; the paper also developed a prompt framework for using ChatGPT in this context.

findings.finding_summary: In the experimental comparison of traditional versus ChatGPT-assisted lesson plans, ChatGPT-assisted plans received a higher average evaluation score than traditional plans (21.0 vs 17.0). The study reports that ChatGPT significantly improved lesson-planning quality, although the paper does not provide a test statistic or confidence interval in the excerpted text.
findings.measure: Professor-rated lesson plan quality using a six-dimension rubric adapted from the 5E Inquiry Lesson Plan framework
findings.sample_size: n=25 lesson plans (12 traditional, 13 ChatGPT-assisted); n=13 teachers; n=6 professors

findings.finding_summary: Teachers reported that ChatGPT improved lesson-planning efficiency, including faster topic selection, faster generation of instructional content, and reduced planning time. Mean ratings were 3.7 for accelerated topic selection, 3.8 for rapid generation of high-quality instructional content, and 4.2 for reduced lesson-planning time.
findings.measure: Teacher survey ratings on teaching efficiency and time savings

findings.finding_summary: Teachers rated ChatGPT positively for interdisciplinary integration, with 61% of respondents giving ratings of 4 or above on the interdisciplinary items. The paper describes ChatGPT as effective for rapidly generating interdisciplinary teaching resources, but no formal effect size is reported.
findings.measure: Teacher survey ratings on interdisciplinary integration

findings.finding_summary: Teachers generally agreed that ChatGPT improved lesson-plan content quality, including accuracy and alignment with their requirements. The reported average ratings were 4.0 for content accuracy and 3.9 for meeting teacher requirements, but the paper also notes limitations in practicality, personalization, and safety-related suitability.
findings.measure: Teacher survey ratings on content quality and fit to requirements

findings.finding_summary: Teachers were neutral on ChatGPT's ability to foster innovation: the paper states ChatGPT more often served as a source of inspiration than as a generator of wholly innovative content. The study frames this as a limitation of the tool and emphasizes that it cannot replace teachers' own observational and creative work.
findings.measure: Teacher survey ratings and interview themes on innovation

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods experimental study with teacher and professor participants, but it is small and not randomized in the strict RCT sense. The evidence is useful yet limited by feasibility sampling, self-report measures, and the absence of full statistical detail in the excerpt.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gains are practically meaningful for teacher-facing lesson planning, including higher lesson-plan quality scores and improved efficiency. However, the evidence is mostly descriptive and the sample is small, so the overall impact is modest rather than large.
